lessons.title: Your two cards
lessons.summary: Learn that hole cards are private to you until showdown.
objectives: Distinguish hole cards from community cards
Recognize that other seats hide their hole cards

activities.accessibilityText: These two are yours alone. Nobody else sees them.

coachMedia.text: These two are yours alone. Nobody else sees them.

activities.accessibilityText: Choose which pair are your private hole cards.
activities.prompt: Which cards are your hole cards?

coachMedia.text: Look at the two cards in front of you — not the board.

choices.label: Ah Kd in front of you
choices.accessibilityText: Select ace of hearts and king of diamonds as your hole cards.

grading.feedback: Right. Those two stay private until showdown.

choices.label: The flop cards in the middle

grading.feedback: Board cards are shared. Your hole cards sit in front of you.
Those belong to someone else. Yours are the two in front of you.

activities.accessibilityText: Decide who can see your hole cards during the hand.
objectives: Recognize that other seats hide their hole cards
activities.prompt: Who can see your hole cards right now?

choices.label: Only you
choices.accessibilityText: Select that only you see your hole cards.

grading.feedback: Private until showdown. Protect them.

choices.label: Everyone at the table
choices.accessibilityText: Select that the whole table sees your hole cards.

grading.feedback: If everyone saw them, they would not be hole cards.

choices.label: Only the dealer
choices.accessibilityText: Select that only the dealer sees your hole cards.

grading.feedback: Dealers should not peek. Treat the cards as yours alone.
grading.reversalRead: Casino procedures vary; still play as if only you know them.

activities.accessibilityText: Pick the shared community cards on a simple flop.
objectives: Distinguish hole cards from community cards

choices.label: Qs Jh 2c in the middle
choices.accessibilityText: Select the queen, jack, and deuce in the middle.

grading.feedback: Those are shared. Everyone uses them.

choices.label: Your Ah Kd
choices.accessibilityText: Select your ace-king as community cards.

grading.feedback: Those stay yours. Community cards are in the middle.

choices.label: Folded cards in the muck
choices.accessibilityText: Select folded cards in the muck.

grading.feedback: Mucked cards are dead, not the board.

activities.accessibilityText: On a fuller table, identify your private hole cards again.
objectives: Distinguish hole cards from community cards
activities.prompt: Six seats, flop out. Which cards are only yours?

choices.label: The two cards at your seat
choices.accessibilityText: Select the two cards at your seat.

grading.feedback: Still just your two. Board and other seats stay separate.

choices.label: Flop plus your two cards
choices.accessibilityText: Select the flop plus your hole cards.

grading.feedback: You combine them later to make a hand. Ownership stays split.
grading.reversalRead: At showdown you reveal them, but until then they are private.

choices.label: Every face-up card you can see
choices.accessibilityText: Select every face-up card in view.

grading.feedback: You can see the board, but those cards are not yours alone.

activities.accessibilityText: Put preflop action seats in order after the big blind.
activities.prompt: Order the first three seats to act preflop after the blinds post.

correct.feedback: UTG acts first. Button acts last.

incorrect.feedback: Start under the gun, then move toward the button.

activities.accessibilityText: Enter the pot size after a three-big-blind open into a one-big-blind pot.

numericPrompt.question: Blinds are 1/2. Nobody limps. BTN opens to 6. What is the pot before the blinds act?

grading.feedback: 1 + 2 + 6 = 9 chips in the middle.

missGrading.feedback: Add both blinds and the open: 1 + 2 + 6.

activities.accessibilityText: Choose whether to open or fold UTG with seven-two offsuit.
activities.prompt: You are UTG with 72o at 1/2. What do you do?

grading.feedback: Trash from early position is an easy fold.
Seventy-two offsuit is not an open from UTG.
Limping junk builds multiway pots you do not want.

activities.accessibilityText: Rank three starting hands from strongest to weakest for an early-position open.
activities.prompt: Rank these UTG open candidates from strongest to weakest.

correct.feedback: Premium pair, then strong broadway, then trash.

incorrect.feedback: Aces lead. Suited ace next. Seventy-two is last.

activities.accessibilityText: Play a short scripted live cash hand as the big blind.
activities.prompt: Defend or fold this big-blind hand.

grading.feedback: Folding A7o is fine; defending is optional this deep.
A call keeps the hand playable in position later.
Jamming A7o for 100bb is a clear mistake.

decisionPoints.prompt: BTN opens to 6. You hold A7o in the big blind. What do you do?

grading.feedback: Folding A7o is fine; defending is optional this deep.
A call keeps the hand playable in position later.
Jamming A7o for 100bb is a clear mistake.
